title: Using your infusion pump
summary: Step-by-step operating guidelines, alarm troubleshooting, and battery maintenance for ambulatory CADD-Solis pump units.

pages.title: Clinical Setup & Inspection
content: Before handling the pump or medication cassette, thoroughly wash hands with warm water and antimicrobial soap for at least 30 seconds.
Verify that the medication cassette label matches your full name, prescribed medication, and infusion rate.
Inspect the cassette latch mechanism. Ensure the flow stop clip is open before inserting tubing into the pump channel.
Check battery indicator on the top-right LCD screen. If below 2 bars, replace with four fresh alkaline AA batteries immediately.
pages.callout: Never force the cassette latch. If resistance is met, inspect tubing orientation.

pages.title: Priming & Tubing Connection
content: Power on the device using the recessed switch on the right side panel.
Press the PRIME key on the keypad. Confirm on-screen prompt: 'Prime tubing now?'.
Hold the prime button until fluid droplets emerge from the distal luer-lock tip without bubbles.
Inspect the entire line against a contrasting surface to confirm no micro-air pockets remain.
Connect securely to your intravenous access port using the aseptic non-touch technique (ANTT).
pages.callout: If air bubble exceeds 2 cm in tubing, re-prime line before connecting to patient catheter.

pages.title: Alarm Responses & Troubleshooting
content: High Pressure / Occlusion Alarm: Check tubing for kinks, closed clamps, or patient posture shifts compressing the lumen.
Air-in-Line Alarm: Inspect the air detector sensor recess. Wipe optical lens with alcohol wipe. Disconnect and aspirate if air detected.
Upstream Occlusion Alarm: Ensure the medication reservoir bag vent is open and fluid is not depleted.
System Fault Code 900+: Power unit off, wait 10 seconds, reboot. If error persists, call clinical after-hours immediately.
pages.callout: Never silence an occlusion alarm repeatedly without physically inspecting the IV line.

pages.title: Emergency Disconnect & Daily Storage
content: To pause infusion for dressing change or emergency: press STOP, clamp the line clamp closest to the cannula, and disconnect luer.
Place a sterile cap on both the pump line tip and the catheter extension lumen.
Store the pump in the provided water-resistant shoulder holster during ambulation.
Keep pump away from direct heat sources, open flame, and electromagnetic interference.
Record remaining volume on your clinical daily tracking sheet every morning at 09:00.
pages.callout: For unresolved alarms between 5:00 PM and 8:00 AM, use the Clinical After Hours Support button.

title: Injection technique: step by step
summary: Subcutaneous injection instructions for enoxaparin, insulin, and biologic therapies with anatomical site rotation.

pages.title: Preparation & Site Selection
content: Clean a clean, dry table surface with a disinfectant wipe. Gather syringe, 2 alcohol swabs, and sharps container.
Verify the medication name, dose, expiry date, and appearance (clear solution, free of cloudiness or particulate).
Recommended sites: Lower abdomen (at least 5 cm / 2 inches away from navel), outer thighs, or back of upper arms.
Maintain a rotation log: never inject into the identical site twice in a 7-day period to prevent lipohypertrophy.
pages.callout: Do not inject into bruised, tender, red, or scarred skin.

pages.title: Aspiration & Administration
content: Swab injection site with alcohol in an outward spiral motion. Allow skin to air-dry completely for 15 seconds.
Gently pinch a 2-inch fold of skin between thumb and index finger to lift subcutaneous tissue from muscle.
Insert needle swiftly at a 90-degree angle (or 45-degree angle if very lean body habitus).
Depress plunger smoothly and steadily until all medication is delivered.
Wait 5 seconds before releasing skin pinch and withdrawing the needle straight out.
pages.callout: For prefilled enoxaparin syringes: do not expel the tiny air bubble prior to injection.

pages.title: Post-Injection Care & Disposal
content: Apply gentle pressure with dry sterile gauze for 10 seconds. Do not massage or rub the injection site.
Activate safety needle shield immediately until a distinct click is heard.
Drop syringe directly into your approved yellow biohazard sharps container. Never recap a used needle.
Record injection date, time, site abbreviation (e.g., L-ABD, R-THIGH), and dosage in your patient handbook.
pages.callout: When your sharps container reaches the 'Full' fill line, seal permanently and contact clinic for exchange.

title: Caring for your PICC line dressing
summary: Maintenance of central venous line transparent dressings, biopatch checks, and signs of catheter-related bloodstream infection.

pages.title: Dressing Assessment Criteria
content: Your transparent PICC dressing must remain completely clean, dry, and intact (CDI) at all times.
Inspect dressing visually twice daily: once in the morning and once before retiring for bed.
Check the chlorhexidine gluconate (CHG) biopatch sponge: blue grid side must face upwards toward ceiling.
Confirm catheter external measurement markings match your discharge card (e.g. 3 cm visible external length).
pages.callout: If external catheter length has shifted by more than 2 cm, call nursing triage immediately.

pages.title: Showering & Moisture Protection
content: Never submerge the PICC arm in bath water, swimming pools, or hot tubs.
Wrap arm thoroughly with plastic cling wrap extending 4 inches above and below the dressing perimeter.
Secure edges with waterproof medical tape or slide a certified silicone shower sleeve over the arm.
Keep arm angled away from direct shower spray. Inspect immediately after shower for moisture infiltration.
pages.callout: If water breaches dressing, it must be changed by nursing staff within 4 hours to prevent bacteremia.

pages.title: Signs of Complication & Infection
content: Erythema: Redness spreading outward along vein tract (cord sign).
Swelling / Edema: Arm or neck circumference noticeably increased on the catheter side.
Pain or tenderness along inner arm, shoulder, or chest wall.
Exudate: Yellow, green, or cloudy discharge visible under transparent dressing window.
Systemic fever: Body temperature above 38.0°C (100.4°F), rigors, or sudden shivering.
pages.callout: Sudden fever with chills in a PICC patient is a medical emergency. Call after-hours triage immediately.

pages.title: Weekly Nurse Visit Handover
content: Home nursing visits occur weekly (every 7 days) for sterile dressing, biopatch, and StatLock stabilization replacement.
Maintain PICC care kit box in a cool, dry area away from pets and children.
Ensure catheter clamps remain locked whenever the line is not in active infusion use.
Contact the clinic 48 hours prior if you need additional saline flushes or alcohol disinfection caps.
pages.callout: Do not attempt to change the sterile PICC dressing yourself unless specifically trained by our clinical team.

title: When to call versus go to the ER
summary: Triage guidance distinguishing life-threatening emergencies requiring 911/ER from urgent after-hours clinic telephone triage.

pages.title: Emergency: Call 911 / Hospital ER
content: Acute chest pain, pressure, or tightness radiating to jaw, neck, back, or left arm.
Sudden shortness of breath, gasping, or inability to speak in complete sentences.
Signs of stroke: Facial drooping, arm weakness or numbness, slurred speech (FAST criteria).
Severe sudden hemorrhage or uncontrolled bleeding not stopping after 10 minutes of direct pressure.
Sudden confusion, loss of consciousness, seizures, or severe anaphylactic allergic swelling.
pages.callout: Do NOT use this web portal for 911 emergencies. Dial 911 immediately or proceed to nearest Emergency Department.

pages.title: Clinic After Hours Support
content: Infusion pump alarms that cannot be cleared following standard protocol.
Catheter insertion site redness, slight seepage, or dressing detachment.
Medication adverse effects: mild nausea, dizziness, missed dose guidance, or rash without respiratory symptoms.
Urgent prescription refill required overnight to prevent critical dose interruption.
Clinician is reachable 5:00 PM – 8:00 AM weekdays and 24 hours on weekends via the After Hours tab.
pages.callout: Submitting the After Hours form logs your clinical issue and opens direct telephone connection to our on-call clinician.

title: Storing medications at home
summary: Temperature monitoring guidelines, refrigeration protocols (2°C to 8°C), and light protection for clinical pharmaceuticals.

pages.title: Temperature Controlled Storage
content: Refrigerated medications (insulin, biologics, reconstituted antibiotics) must remain between 2°C and 8°C (36°F to 46°F).
Place medications on the middle refrigerator shelf. Never store inside door bins (temperature fluctuates with opening).
Never store directly adjacent to refrigerator freezer chiller vents to prevent accidental freezing.
Frozen medications must be discarded even if thawed, as peptide structures denature upon freezing.
pages.callout: Use a dedicated refrigerator thermometer and check dial reading daily.

pages.title: Room Temperature & Ambient Guidelines
content: Controlled room temperature is defined as 15°C to 25°C (59°F to 77°F).
Do not store oral tablets in bathroom medicine cabinets due to high steam humidity and thermal cycling.
Keep original amber bottles tightly closed to protect hygroscopic compounds from ambient moisture.
Protect light-sensitive injectables in their protective cardboard cartons until immediate moment of use.
pages.callout: During summer heatwaves without air conditioning, consult the pharmacy for temporary cool-pack storage guidance.

pages.title: Travel & Power Outage Protocol
content: When traveling by automobile or aircraft, carry all medications in insulated cooler bags with gel ice packs.
Never pack vital clinical medications in airline checked luggage; always carry in personal cabin baggage.
During home power outages exceeding 4 hours: keep refrigerator door sealed to conserve thermal mass.
If outage exceeds 12 hours, call clinic pharmacy to assess medication viability before administering.
pages.callout: We provide emergency power backup advisories for clients on continuous mechanical infusion therapy.

title: Sharps disposal
summary: Safe handling of used needles, lancets, and infusion stylets in compliance with provincial biohazardous waste regulations.

pages.title: Sharps Safety Rules
content: Immediately drop used needles, syringes, and infusion cannulae into an approved rigid puncture-proof sharps container.
Never bend, break, shear, or recap needles by hand under any circumstances.
Keep sharps containers at eye level, stable, and out of reach of household pets and young children.
Do not force items into the container opening. Never insert fingers into the container aperture.
pages.callout: Needlestick injuries require immediate soap washing and 24/7 post-exposure prophylaxis triage.

pages.title: Container Sealing & Clinic Return
content: When contents reach the 3/4 fill indicator line, engage the irreversible locking lid mechanism until it snaps.
Wipe outer exterior of container with a hospital-grade disinfectant wipe.
Bring sealed container to Harbourline clinic reception or participating community pharmacy depot for safe incineration.
Never place loose or bottled sharps in municipal household garbage, blue recycling bins, or compost bins.
pages.callout: Need replacement sharps containers? Request through the Request Documents & Supplies menu or call our office.
